inline_comments.comment: Six imports are declared in this file but never used: `readFileSync` and `writeFileSync` (line 1), `find` from `empathic/find` (line 3), `detectIndent` (line 4), `join` from `pathe` (line 5), and `getProjectRoot` (line 7). None of the functions defined in this module (`formatMinVersion`, `isNodeVersionSupported`, `parseNodeVersionString`) reference any of these. They appear to be leftovers from an incomplete or partially-reverted implementation. They should be removed; their presence is confirmed as accidental by the test file, which has to mock three of the corresponding modules (`empathic/find`, `node:fs`, `utils/paths.ts`) purely to neutralize side effects of the dead imports.

`maxDefinedMajor` is recomputed via `Math.max(...MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_VERSIONS.map(...))` on every call to `isNodeVersionSupported`. Because `MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_VERSIONS` is a module-level constant, this value never changes at runtime. Move it to a module-level constant (e.g., `const MAX_DEFINED_MAJOR = Math.max(...MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_VERSIONS.map((v) => v.major));`) so the computation runs only once.

`export {}` is a non-obvious TypeScript idiom. Without any explanation, a reader unfamiliar with the pattern may not understand why it is here. It marks the file as an ES module, which is required to enable top-level `await` when there are no other static `import` or `export` statements. A short inline comment (e.g., `// Marks this file as an ES module so top-level await is valid`) would make the intent immediately clear.

`MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_DESCRIPTION` is fetched with a second `await import('storybook/internal/common')` call, separate from the one on line 4 that already loaded `isNodeVersionSupported` from the same module. While Node's module cache makes this a no-op at runtime, structurally it gives the false impression that two separate loads are happening and makes the code harder to follow. Destructure both exports from the single first import: `const { isNodeVersionSupported, MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_DESCRIPTION } = await import('storybook/internal/common');`.

The error message in this file was trimmed to remove the closing sentence "Please upgrade your Node.js installation." The equivalent messages in `code/core/src/bin/dispatcher.ts` and `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/bin/index.ts` still include that sentence. This creates an inconsistent user experience depending on which binary surface triggers the version check. The omission appears unintentional given all three files were refactored together.

`logger.outro('')` is called with an empty string immediately before `process.exit(1)`. `outro` is a clack UI primitive that renders a visual closing frame. Calling it with an empty string produces a bare closing glyph with no message, whose purpose is not obvious here — especially since the process exits right after and the other two bin entry points (`dispatcher.ts`, `cli-storybook/bin/index.ts`) do not make this call. If there is a specific reason (e.g., to close a previously opened `intro` frame in some code path), a comment explaining it would help; otherwise, consider removing it for consistency.

`'yarn' as PackageManagerName` is an incorrect type assertion. `PackageManagerName` is a string enum whose members are `'npm'`, `'yarn1'`, `'yarn2'`, `'pnpm'`, and `'bun'` — there is no `'yarn'` member. The assertion forces TypeScript to accept an invalid value, silently misrepresenting the enum. The previous `as any` was at least transparent about bypassing the type system. The correct fix is to use the actual enum member `PackageManagerName.YARN1` (value `'yarn1'`) if that is the intended behavior; the corresponding `expect` on line 106 should then assert `force: PackageManagerName.YARN1` to keep the test self-consistent.

general_comments.comment: The new `isNodeVersionSupported` function quietly changes the rejection behavior for odd-numbered Node.js major versions. Under the original inline checks, a runtime running Node 21 (or any other even-gapped major not explicitly enumerated) would pass the guard because it was neither below 20 nor equal to 22 with a low minor. Under the new implementation, any major that does not appear in `MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_VERSIONS` and is not above the highest defined major is rejected. Node 21 is EOL, so rejecting it is arguably correct, but the behavioral difference is undocumented. A brief comment in `node-version.ts` noting that only even LTS majors (and future majors above the highest defined) are accepted would prevent confusion when someone later investigates why Node 21 was not accepted.

The test file `node-version.test.ts` mocks `empathic/find`, `node:fs`, and `./utils/paths.ts` at the top of the suite. Inspecting the source module, none of the exported functions actually use those imports — the mocks exist purely to suppress side effects from the dead imports. If the unused imports are removed from `node-version.ts` (see inline comment), all three mocks can also be removed, making the tests simpler and removing a coupling that would confuse future maintainers.
